(For R2 & R3) : Mr.T.Arun Kumar

ORDER The writ petition is filed seeking direction to the 3rd respondent not to take any action in violation of The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and The Food Safety and Standards Regulations, 2010,
and the Indian Standards Institutions (Certification Marks) Act, and direct the 1st respondent to issue appropriate directions to the 2nd and 3rd respondent to forbid from taking any action in an arbitrary manner.
2.With reference to the relief sought in the writ petition, undoubtedly the authorities are not expected to act in an arbitrary https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis manner.
Equally, the authorities are duty bound to conduct inspections by following the procedures as contemplated under the the Food Safety Act.
Lawful entry, inspections and inquiry contemplated under the Food Safety Act cannot be interfered by the Courts.
Authorities, on information or based on the complaints, are empowered to conduct inspections, inquiry etc., in order to maintain the food standards under the provisions of the Food Safety Act.
Thus, the relief sought in general cannot be granted.

If at all, any arbitrary action or corrupt activities of the officials are noticed, then the petitioner is at liberty to file a complaint before the competent authorities for initiation of action against the officials.

3.However, the inspections, inquiry etc. if any conducted by the authorities by following the procedures cannot be interfered with by the Courts and thus, the relief as such sought for in the writ petition is not entertainable.

If at all, the petitioner has suffered from any corrupt activity or illegality or otherwise, then he is at liberty to file an appropriate complaint before the competent authorities for initiation of action against the concerned officials.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
4.Accordingly, the Writ Petition stands disposed of.
No costs.
In view of the disposal of the writ petition, the Review Application also stands closed.
